notice: Notice: these results come from a scripted agent that replays fixed trajectories; no model was called. They measure harness mechanics only. Exercised for real: the context manager, the execution guard, the model router and the local decision policy (classification, strategy, escalation decisions). Scripted or reimplemented by the harness itself, not run through the orchestration engine: the attempt loop and retries, task scheduling and parallelism, and whether a step or a verification passes. No command is executed, and the engine's run and task flow, baselines, approvals, permission policy and verification engine are not exercised. Cost and duration are simulated units. The results are not evidence about the performance of any model or of the engine's orchestration. Scripted results say nothing about model quality, and tool-definition token figures are estimates from rough constants, not measurements.

configs.description: Reference point: planning on, elision, 3 attempts, sequential, policy routing, guard on.
No plan: subtasks run in declaration order with no dependency resolution.
Plan only when the local decision policy asks for one.
Unmanaged context: nothing is ever compacted.
Elision that starts early and protects no recent tool output.
Elision, then summarization by a stub that truncates. The summarizer is a stub, not a model.
Every attempt at the standard tier.
Every attempt at the premium tier.
Up to 3 subtasks at once when the plan and the decision policy allow it.
Every guard rule disabled; only the attempt limit bounds a loop.
Capability profile of an economy executor: plan for anything above trivial, structured tools, every attempt at the economy tier.
Capability profile of a premium executor: plan only from moderate complexity up or above low risk, lean tools, every attempt at the premium tier.
Lean tool profile: the reference agent is offered the shell plus one read and one edit tool. The script calls no tool, so only the listed tools differ.
Per-task tool selection off: every subtask is handed the reference agent's whole tool list. Same settings as baseline, named to be read next to tools-selection-local.

Per-task tool selection by the local policy: each subtask is handed the floor plus the tools its text gives a reason for. A scripted step whose tool was dropped records a miss and the tool is restored. Token figures are estimates from rough per-tool constants.
